blocks.text:
Confirmed: tag-chain jobs (integration, publish, binaries, web-spa, release-provenance, install-pin-bump, installer-smoke) all gate on `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` or release events — schedule ref is `refs/heads/main` → they skip on schedule ✓ (leave untouched). js-ext-integration — need to check its if. Let me check line ~2909.

binaries-pr: if PR||dispatch — skips on schedule ✓.

js-ext-integration at 2909: from the earlier if-listing it printed `js-ext-integration: needs: quality-gate` with no if → runs whenever quality-gate succeeds! On schedule non-empty tick today, does js-ext-integration run? Its needs quality-gate succeeds on schedule → it RUNS on schedule runs today. Hmm — so it's part of the schedule run. On empty tick: quality-gate skipped → js-ext-integration has no custom if → implicit success() → skipped ✓ automatically. OK but should I guard it explicitly? Auto-skip works. Leave it? For robustness/uniformity... I'll guard it too since it executes on schedule (it's effectively a gate leg). Actually wait — its needs is only quality-gate; when quality-gate is SKIPPED, jobs needing it without custom if are skipped ✓. Fine either way. I'll add the guard for explicitness — hmm, but the ticket says keep tag/release arms untouched; js-ext is not tag-gated at all. Adding release-pending to its needs is harmless. Let me add it — no wait. Minimal diff vs uniformity. The test will define the contract; let me include js-ext-integration in the guarded set since it runs on schedule.

Hmm, actually let me not over-engineer. Guard set (final):

In quality-gate closure (needs release-pending + pending guard in if):
changes, cube-kernel-live, static, test-core, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, flutter-app-exzone, app-crap-gate, test-faui, faui-coverage, cli-visual-settings, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, perf-gate, usage-fold, quality-gate.
Plus: step-timings, release, js-ext-integration.

That's the full set. Jobs explicitly NOT guarded (with reason): watchdog (PR-only if), ci-red-report (push-only if), binaries-pr (PR||dispatch if), binaries-smoke-gate (PR||dispatch if), and the tag/release-chain (integration, publish, binaries, web-spa, release-provenance, install-pin-bump, installer-smoke — all tags/release-event gated).

Wait, on empty tick: `integration` (needs quality-gate, custom if false on schedule) → skipped ✓. publish needs [quality-gate, integration] — custom if false ✓. binaries ✓. web-spa needs quality-gate, if false ✓. release-provenance needs [binaries, web-spa] both skipped + custom if false ✓. install-pin-bump needs release-provenance + if ✓. installer-smoke ✓.

But one hole: `integration`'s custom if: `!cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' && push && tags`. On empty schedule tick: push false → skip ✓.

Also `ci-red-report`: `always() && push && gate=='failure'` → schedule → false ✓.

Now the YAML for each edit. Plan the exact edits:

**1. Header comment + schedule trigger comment** (lines ~45-50):

Current:
```yaml
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 *'
```
Add gh-1551 note.

**2. New job release-pending** — insert right before `changes:` job (after the SEC-08 permissions block). Also the big header comment block (Issue #177 overview) lists jobs — add a line about release-pending.

Job definition:

```yaml
  # ─────────────────
  # gh-1551: the 2h schedule tick is the release-arming mechanism (gh-1537
  # retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with ZERO commits on main
  # since the last v* tag has nothing to release — running the full ~35-40
  # min quality gate for it is pure waste (observed: run 38147581679). This
  # cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout + git rev-list) compares main
  # HEAD against the latest v* tag and exports `pending`; every gate leg
  # ANDs the output into its `if`, so an empty tick short-circuits the whole

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-shot: wire the gh-1551 release-pending guard into ci.yml gate legs."""
import re, sys

path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')

GUARD = "needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
COMMENT = ('    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* '
           'tag)\n    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check '
           'decides.')

# job -> ('and' | 'new' | 'fold_wrap' | 'always_and')
plan = {
    'cube-kernel-live': 'and',
    'static': 'new',
    'test-core': 'new',
    'integration-mock': 'and',
    'hostile-env': 'and',
    'fa-aot-build': 'new_noneeds',
    'pty-integration-linux': 'new',
    'pty-coverage-gate': 'new',
    'pty-visual': 'new',
    'coverage-gate': 'new',
    'guards': 'new',
    'flutter-analyze': 'and',
    'flutter-tests': 'and',
    'flutter-app-exzone': 'fold_wrap',
    'app-crap-gate': 'and',
    'test-faui': 'and',
    'faui-coverage': 'new',
    'cli-visual-settings': 'and',
    'build-web': 'and',
    'build-android': 'and',
    'build-ios': 'and',
    'build-macos': 'and',
    'supply-chain': 'new',
    'dep-audit': 'new',
    'installer-verify': 'new',
    'install-pin-gate': 'new',
    'quality-gate': 'always_and',
    'perf-gate': 'and',
    'usage-fold': 'fold_wrap',
    'step-timings': 'always_and',
    'js-ext-integration': 'new',
    'release': 'release_fold',
}

# find job header line indices
headers = {}
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r'^  ([a-z0-9-]+):$', l)
    if m:
        headers[m.group(1)] = i

def find_line(start, indent, key):
    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
        if re.match(r'^  [a-z0-9-]+:$', lines[j]) and j > start:
            return None
        if lines[j].startswith(f'{indent}{key}:'):
            return j
    return None

edits = []  # (lineno, kind, payload)

for job, mode in plan.items():
    h = headers[job]
    nline = find_line(h, '    ', 'needs')
    iline = find_line(h, '    ', 'if')
    if nline is None:
        if mode == 'new_noneeds':
            edits.append((h + 1, 'insert', f'    needs: release-pending'))
        else:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: expected a needs line')
    else:
        cur = lines[nline].strip()[len('needs:'):].strip()
        if 'release-pending' in cur:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: already wired?')
        if cur.startswith('['):
            new = 'needs: [release-pending, ' + cur[1:]
        else:

        edits.append((nline, 'replace', new))

        edits.append((target, 'insert_after',

    elif mode == 'always_and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()

    elif mode == 'fold_wrap':

        for kind, payload in by_line[i]:

    result.append(line)

i = 0
n = len(lines)

    line = lines[i]
    if i in by_line:
        ops = by_line[i]
        indent = '    '
        replaced = None
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'replace':
                # preserve original indentation of the anchor line
                orig_indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('needs:'):

            result.append(replaced)
        else:
            result.append(line)
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'insert':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
            elif kind == 'insert_after':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
        i += 1
        continue
    result.append(line)
    i += 1

open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(result))

+  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
+  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
+  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
+  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
+  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
+  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
+  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
+  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
+  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
+  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
+  # run stays green.
+  #
+  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
+  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
+  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
+  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
+  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
+  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
+  #
+  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
+  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
+  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
+  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
+  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
+  # does, which is honest.
+  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

+    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)

+    outputs:

+      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.

+              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"

There's a BUG: `||` expressions got the guard appended without parentheses:

`needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`

Due to `&&` binding tighter than `||`, this evaluates as `core || (shared && pending)` — WRONG! If core=true and pending=false, the leg would still RUN. Must wrap: `(core || shared) && pending`.

Affected jobs with `||` in single-line ifs: hostile-env, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, cli-visual-settings, build-web/android/ios/macos. integration-mock has no `||` (single condition) ✓. cube-kernel-live single ✓.

Fix: wrap the original expression in parens.

{"newText":"jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410b181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Now the mechanical per-job edits. Rather than 30 individual edit calls with exact context, a Python script might be more reliable — but the instructions favor precision. Actually a script that does targeted regex replacements per job with verification is efficient. Let me write a Python script that:

For each target job, finds the job block, and:
1. Replaces `needs: X` line with `needs: [release-pending, X]` (or adds `needs: release-pending` if no needs).
2. Modifies/adds `if:`.

The if handling varies:
- No if → insert `if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` after the needs line (with a short comment).
- Single-line if `if: <expr>` → `if: <expr> && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`.
- `if: always()` → `if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`.
- Folded `if: >-` blocks: append the clause as a new last line.

Jobs and their handling:
- cube-kernel-live: needs changes; if single line → AND.
- static: needs changes; no if → add.
- test-core: needs changes; no if → add.
- integration-mock: AND.
- hostile-env: AND (single line).
- fa-aot-build: no needs; add needs + if.
- pty-integration-linux: needs [fa-aot-build]; no if → add.
- pty-coverage-gate: needs [pty-integration-linux]; no if → add.
- pty-visual: needs changes; no if → add.
- coverage-gate: needs [changes, test-core]; no if → add.
- guards: needs [changes, test-core]; no if → add.
- flutter-analyze: AND.
- flutter-tests: AND.
- flutter-app-exzone: folded if → append line `      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` — wait, folded `>-` with `||` structure: append `&& (...)`? The block is:
```
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
```
Appending `&&` to the last line works: `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && needs...` — but precedence: `A || B && C` parses as `A || (B && C)` — wrong! Need parentheses: change last line to `(github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`? Still `A || (B && C && D)` — WRONG. Must wrap the whole expression: append a line `      ) && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` with an opening paren added to the first line. Simplest: modify first line to start with `(` and last line append `&& needs...` preceded by closing paren:
```
    if: >-
      ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
```

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-shot: wire the gh-1551 release-pending guard into ci.yml gate legs."""
import re, sys

path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')

GUARD = "needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
COMMENT = ('    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* '
           'tag)\n    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check '
           'decides.')

# job -> ('and' | 'new' | 'fold_wrap' | 'always_and')
plan = {
    'cube-kernel-live': 'and',
    'static': 'new',
    'test-core': 'new',
    'integration-mock': 'and',
    'hostile-env': 'and',
    'fa-aot-build': 'new_noneeds',
    'pty-integration-linux': 'new',
    'pty-coverage-gate': 'new',
    'pty-visual': 'new',
    'coverage-gate': 'new',
    'guards': 'new',
    'flutter-analyze': 'and',
    'flutter-tests': 'and',
    'flutter-app-exzone': 'fold_wrap',
    'app-crap-gate': 'and',
    'test-faui': 'and',
    'faui-coverage': 'new',
    'cli-visual-settings': 'and',
    'build-web': 'and',
    'build-android': 'and',
    'build-ios': 'and',
    'build-macos': 'and',
    'supply-chain': 'new',
    'dep-audit': 'new',
    'installer-verify': 'new',
    'install-pin-gate': 'new',
    'quality-gate': 'always_and',
    'perf-gate': 'and',
    'usage-fold': 'fold_wrap',
    'step-timings': 'always_and',
    'js-ext-integration': 'new',
    'release': 'release_fold',
}

# find job header line indices
headers = {}
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r'^  ([a-z0-9-]+):$', l)
    if m:
        headers[m.group(1)] = i

def find_line(start, indent, key):
    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
        if re.match(r'^  [a-z0-9-]+:$', lines[j]) and j > start:
            return None
        if lines[j].startswith(f'{indent}{key}:'):
            return j
    return None

edits = []  # (lineno, kind, payload)

for job, mode in plan.items():
    h = headers[job]
    nline = find_line(h, '    ', 'needs')
    iline = find_line(h, '    ', 'if')
    if nline is None:
        if mode == 'new_noneeds':
            edits.append((h + 1, 'insert', f'    needs: release-pending'))
        else:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: expected a needs line')
    else:
        cur = lines[nline].strip()[len('needs:'):].strip()
        if 'release-pending' in cur:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: already wired?')
        if cur.startswith('['):
            new = 'needs: [release-pending, ' + cur[1:]
        else:
            new = f'needs: [release-pending, {cur}]'
        edits.append((nline, 'replace', new))

    if mode == 'and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur.startswith('if:'), cur
        expr = cur[len('if:'):].strip()
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: {expr} && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode in ('new', 'new_noneeds'):
        target = nline if nline is not None else h + 1
        edits.append((target, 'insert_after',
                      f'{COMMENT}\n    if: {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'always_and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur == 'if: always()', cur
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: always() && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'fold_wrap':
        assert lines[iline].strip() == 'if: >-', (job, lines[iline])
        # find block extent
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        first_expr = iline + 1
        edits.append((first_expr, 'replace',
                      '(' + lines[first_expr].strip()))
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ') &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'release_fold':
        # append guard as a new folded line at the end of the if block
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ' &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    else:
        sys.exit(f'unknown mode {mode}')

# apply edits bottom-up, tracking insert positions
edits.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], 0 if e[1] == 'replace' else 1))
out = list(lines)
for lineno, kind, payload in sorted(edits, key=lambda e: -e[0] if e[1] == 'replace' else -(e[0] + 0.5)):
    pass  # handled below

# Simpler: apply in reverse line order; inserts before/after anchored at the
# (possibly already edited) line. Since replace and insert share anchors,
# process per anchor in a stable way.
from collections import defaultdict
by_line = defaultdict(list)
for lineno, kind, payload in edits:
    by_line[lineno].append((kind, payload))

result = []
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if i in by_line:
        for kind, payload in by_line[i]:
            if kind == 'replace':
                line = '    ' + payload if not payload.startswith('    ') else payload
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('(') or payload.lstrip().startswith('needs.'):
                    line = '      ' + payload if 'needs.' in payload[:8] or payload.lstrip().startswith('(') else '    ' + payload
            # collects handled below
        # re-derive: we must keep replace-1 + insert_after ordering
    result.append(line)

# The above in-place juggling is error-prone; rebuild cleanly instead.
result = []
i = 0
n = len(lines)
while i < n:
    line = lines[i]
    if i in by_line:
        ops = by_line[i]
        indent = '    '
        replaced = None
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'replace':
                # preserve original indentation of the anchor line
                orig_indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('needs:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                elif payload.lstrip().startswith('if:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                else:
                    # folded if expression line: 6-space indent
                    replaced = f'      {payload}'
        if replaced is not None:
            result.append(replaced)
        else:
            result.append(line)
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'insert':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
            elif kind == 'insert_after':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
        i += 1
        continue
    result.append(line)
    i += 1

open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(result))
print('applied', len(edits), 'edits across', len(plan), 'jobs')
","path":"/tmp/wire_guard.py"}

+  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
+  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
+  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
+  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
+  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run

+  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
+  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
+  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the

There's a BUG: `||` expressions got the guard appended without parentheses:

`needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`

Due to `&&` binding tighter than `||`, this evaluates as `core || (shared && pending)` — WRONG! If core=true and pending=false, the leg would still RUN. Must wrap: `(core || shared) && pending`.

Affected jobs with `||` in single-line ifs: hostile-env, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, cli-visual-settings, build-web/android/ios/macos. integration-mock has no `||` (single condition) ✓. cube-kernel-live single ✓.

Fix: wrap the original expression in parens.

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')
fixed = 0
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r"^(    if: )(.+) && needs\.release-pending\.outputs\.pending == 'true'$", l)
    if m and ' || ' in m.group(2) and not m.group(2).startswith('('):
        lines[i] = f"{m.group(1)}({m.group(2)}) && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
        fixed += 1
open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
print('fixed', fixed)
EOF"}

{"newText":"jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410b181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-shot: wire the gh-1551 release-pending guard into ci.yml gate legs."""
import re, sys

path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')

GUARD = "needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
COMMENT = ('    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* '
           'tag)\n    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check '
           'decides.')

# job -> ('and' | 'new' | 'fold_wrap' | 'always_and')
plan = {
    'cube-kernel-live': 'and',
    'static': 'new',
    'test-core': 'new',
    'integration-mock': 'and',
    'hostile-env': 'and',
    'fa-aot-build': 'new_noneeds',
    'pty-integration-linux': 'new',
    'pty-coverage-gate': 'new',
    'pty-visual': 'new',
    'coverage-gate': 'new',
    'guards': 'new',
    'flutter-analyze': 'and',
    'flutter-tests': 'and',
    'flutter-app-exzone': 'fold_wrap',
    'app-crap-gate': 'and',
    'test-faui': 'and',
    'faui-coverage': 'new',
    'cli-visual-settings': 'and',
    'build-web': 'and',
    'build-android': 'and',
    'build-ios': 'and',
    'build-macos': 'and',
    'supply-chain': 'new',
    'dep-audit': 'new',
    'installer-verify': 'new',
    'install-pin-gate': 'new',
    'quality-gate': 'always_and',
    'perf-gate': 'and',
    'usage-fold': 'fold_wrap',
    'step-timings': 'always_and',
    'js-ext-integration': 'new',
    'release': 'release_fold',
}

# find job header line indices
headers = {}
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r'^  ([a-z0-9-]+):$', l)
    if m:
        headers[m.group(1)] = i

def find_line(start, indent, key):
    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
        if re.match(r'^  [a-z0-9-]+:$', lines[j]) and j > start:
            return None
        if lines[j].startswith(f'{indent}{key}:'):
            return j
    return None

edits = []  # (lineno, kind, payload)

for job, mode in plan.items():
    h = headers[job]
    nline = find_line(h, '    ', 'needs')
    iline = find_line(h, '    ', 'if')
    if nline is None:
        if mode == 'new_noneeds':
            edits.append((h + 1, 'insert', f'    needs: release-pending'))
        else:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: expected a needs line')
    else:
        cur = lines[nline].strip()[len('needs:'):].strip()
        if 'release-pending' in cur:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: already wired?')
        if cur.startswith('['):
            new = 'needs: [release-pending, ' + cur[1:]
        else:
            new = f'needs: [release-pending, {cur}]'
        edits.append((nline, 'replace', new))

    if mode == 'and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur.startswith('if:'), cur
        expr = cur[len('if:'):].strip()
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: {expr} && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode in ('new', 'new_noneeds'):
        target = nline if nline is not None else h + 1
        edits.append((target, 'insert_after',
                      f'{COMMENT}\n    if: {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'always_and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur == 'if: always()', cur
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: always() && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'fold_wrap':
        assert lines[iline].strip() == 'if: >-', (job, lines[iline])
        # find block extent
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        first_expr = iline + 1
        edits.append((first_expr, 'replace',
                      '(' + lines[first_expr].strip()))
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ') &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'release_fold':
        # append guard as a new folded line at the end of the if block
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ' &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    else:
        sys.exit(f'unknown mode {mode}')

# apply edits bottom-up, tracking insert positions
edits.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], 0 if e[1] == 'replace' else 1))
out = list(lines)
for lineno, kind, payload in sorted(edits, key=lambda e: -e[0] if e[1] == 'replace' else -(e[0] + 0.5)):
    pass  # handled below

# Simpler: apply in reverse line order; inserts before/after anchored at the
# (possibly already edited) line. Since replace and insert share anchors,
# process per anchor in a stable way.
from collections import defaultdict
by_line = defaultdict(list)
for lineno, kind, payload in edits:
    by_line[lineno].append((kind, payload))

result = []
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if i in by_line:
        for kind, payload in by_line[i]:
            if kind == 'replace':
                line = '    ' + payload if not payload.startswith('    ') else payload
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('(') or payload.lstrip().startswith('needs.'):
                    line = '      ' + payload if 'needs.' in payload[:8] or payload.lstrip().startswith('(') else '    ' + payload
            # collects handled below
        # re-derive: we must keep replace-1 + insert_after ordering
    result.append(line)

# The above in-place juggling is error-prone; rebuild cleanly instead.
result = []
i = 0
n = len(lines)
while i < n:
    line = lines[i]
    if i in by_line:
        ops = by_line[i]
        indent = '    '
        replaced = None
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'replace':
                # preserve original indentation of the anchor line
                orig_indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('needs:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                elif payload.lstrip().startswith('if:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                else:
                    # folded if expression line: 6-space indent
                    replaced = f'      {payload}'
        if replaced is not None:
            result.append(replaced)
        else:
            result.append(line)
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'insert':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
            elif kind == 'insert_after':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
        i += 1
        continue
    result.append(line)
    i += 1

open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(result))
print('applied', len(edits), 'edits across', len(plan), 'jobs')

+  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
+  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
+  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
+  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
+  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
+  # does, which is honest.
+  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+  release-pending:
+    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    outputs:
+      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
+    steps:
+      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
+      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
+      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
+      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410b181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          filter: blob:none
+      - id: check
+        env:
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+        run: |
+          pending=true
+          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
+            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
+            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
+            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
+            # comparison the ticket asks for.
+            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
+            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
+              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
+            else
+              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
+              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
+              echo "latest tag: $latest"
+              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
+              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
+              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
+                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
+                pending=false
+              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
+                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
+              fi
+            fi
+          else
+            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
+          fi
+          echo "release pending: $pending"
+          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
   changes:
     name: Classify changes
     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
+    needs: release-pending
+    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
+    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
+    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
+    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
+    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
+    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
     timeout-minutes: 5

There's a BUG: `||` expressions got the guard appended without parentheses:

`needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`

Due to `&&` binding tighter than `||`, this evaluates as `core || (shared && pending)` — WRONG! If core=true and pending=false, the leg would still RUN. Must wrap: `(core || shared) && pending`.

Affected jobs with `||` in single-line ifs: hostile-env, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, cli-visual-settings, build-web/android/ios/macos. integration-mock has no `||` (single condition) ✓. cube-kernel-live single ✓.

Fix: wrap the original expression in parens.

import re
path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')
fixed = 0
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r"^(    if: )(.+) && needs\.release-pending\.outputs\.pending == 'true'$", l)
    if m and ' || ' in m.group(2) and not m.group(2).startswith('('):
        lines[i] = f"{m.group(1)}({m.group(2)}) && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
        fixed += 1
open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
print('fixed', fixed)
EOF"}

{"newText":"jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410b181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-shot: wire the gh-1551 release-pending guard into ci.yml gate legs."""
import re, sys

path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')

GUARD = "needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
COMMENT = ('    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* '
           'tag)\n    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check '
           'decides.')

# job -> ('and' | 'new' | 'fold_wrap' | 'always_and')
plan = {
    'cube-kernel-live': 'and',
    'static': 'new',
    'test-core': 'new',
    'integration-mock': 'and',
    'hostile-env': 'and',
    'fa-aot-build': 'new_noneeds',
    'pty-integration-linux': 'new',
    'pty-coverage-gate': 'new',
    'pty-visual': 'new',
    'coverage-gate': 'new',
    'guards': 'new',
    'flutter-analyze': 'and',
    'flutter-tests': 'and',
    'flutter-app-exzone': 'fold_wrap',
    'app-crap-gate': 'and',
    'test-faui': 'and',
    'faui-coverage': 'new',
    'cli-visual-settings': 'and',
    'build-web': 'and',
    'build-android': 'and',
    'build-ios': 'and',
    'build-macos': 'and',
    'supply-chain': 'new',
    'dep-audit': 'new',
    'installer-verify': 'new',
    'install-pin-gate': 'new',
    'quality-gate': 'always_and',
    'perf-gate': 'and',
    'usage-fold': 'fold_wrap',
    'step-timings': 'always_and',
    'js-ext-integration': 'new',
    'release': 'release_fold',
}

# find job header line indices
headers = {}
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r'^  ([a-z0-9-]+):$', l)
    if m:
        headers[m.group(1)] = i

def find_line(start, indent, key):
    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
        if re.match(r'^  [a-z0-9-]+:$', lines[j]) and j > start:
            return None
        if lines[j].startswith(f'{indent}{key}:'):
            return j
    return None

edits = []  # (lineno, kind, payload)

for job, mode in plan.items():
    h = headers[job]
    nline = find_line(h, '    ', 'needs')
    iline = find_line(h, '    ', 'if')
    if nline is None:
        if mode == 'new_noneeds':
            edits.append((h + 1, 'insert', f'    needs: release-pending'))
        else:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: expected a needs line')
    else:
        cur = lines[nline].strip()[len('needs:'):].strip()
        if 'release-pending' in cur:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: already wired?')
        if cur.startswith('['):
            new = 'needs: [release-pending, ' + cur[1:]
        else:
            new = f'needs: [release-pending, {cur}]'
        edits.append((nline, 'replace', new))

    if mode == 'and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur.startswith('if:'), cur
        expr = cur[len('if:'):].strip()
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: {expr} && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode in ('new', 'new_noneeds'):
        target = nline if nline is not None else h + 1
        edits.append((target, 'insert_after',
                      f'{COMMENT}\n    if: {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'always_and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur == 'if: always()', cur
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: always() && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'fold_wrap':
        assert lines[iline].strip() == 'if: >-', (job, lines[iline])
        # find block extent
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        first_expr = iline + 1
        edits.append((first_expr, 'replace',
                      '(' + lines[first_expr].strip()))
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ') &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'release_fold':
        # append guard as a new folded line at the end of the if block
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ' &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    else:
        sys.exit(f'unknown mode {mode}')

# apply edits bottom-up, tracking insert positions
edits.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], 0 if e[1] == 'replace' else 1))
out = list(lines)
for lineno, kind, payload in sorted(edits, key=lambda e: -e[0] if e[1] == 'replace' else -(e[0] + 0.5)):
    pass  # handled below

# Simpler: apply in reverse line order; inserts before/after anchored at the
# (possibly already edited) line. Since replace and insert share anchors,
# process per anchor in a stable way.
from collections import defaultdict
by_line = defaultdict(list)
for lineno, kind, payload in edits:
    by_line[lineno].append((kind, payload))

result = []
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if i in by_line:
        for kind, payload in by_line[i]:
            if kind == 'replace':
                line = '    ' + payload if not payload.startswith('    ') else payload
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('(') or payload.lstrip().startswith('needs.'):

+  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
+  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
+  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
+  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
+  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
+  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
+  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
+  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
+  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
+  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
+  # run stays green.
+  #
+  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
+  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
+  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
+  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
+  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
+  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
+  #
+  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
+  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
+  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
+  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
+  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
+  # does, which is honest.
+  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+  release-pending:
+    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    outputs:
+      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
+    steps:
+      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
+      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
+      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
+      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410b181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          filter: blob:none
+      - id: check
+        env:
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+        run: |
+          pending=true
+          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
+            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
+            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
+            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
+            # comparison the ticket asks for.
+            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)

+              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
+              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
+              echo "latest tag: $latest"
+              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
+              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
+              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
+                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"

+              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
+                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
+              fi
+            fi
+          else
+            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
+          fi
+          echo "release pending: $pending"
+          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm

+    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on

There's a BUG: `||` expressions got the guard appended without parentheses:

`needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`

Due to `&&` binding tighter than `||`, this evaluates as `core || (shared && pending)` — WRONG! If core=true and pending=false, the leg would still RUN. Must wrap: `(core || shared) && pending`.

Affected jobs with `||` in single-line ifs: hostile-env, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, cli-visual-settings, build-web/android/ios/macos. integration-mock has no `||` (single condition) ✓. cube-kernel-live single ✓.

Fix: wrap the original expression in parens.

blocks.text: Now the new `release-pending` job, inserted before `changes`:

{"newText":"jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410b181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Now the mechanical per-job edits. Rather than 30 individual edit calls with exact context, a Python script might be more reliable — but the instructions favor precision. Actually a script that does targeted regex replacements per job with verification is efficient. Let me write a Python script that:

For each target job, finds the job block, and:
1. Replaces `needs: X` line with `needs: [release-pending, X]` (or adds `needs: release-pending` if no needs).
2. Modifies/adds `if:`.

The if handling varies:
- No if → insert `if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` after the needs line (with a short comment).
- Single-line if `if: <expr>` → `if: <expr> && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`.
- `if: always()` → `if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`.
- Folded `if: >-` blocks: append the clause as a new last line.

Jobs and their handling:
- cube-kernel-live: needs changes; if single line → AND.
- static: needs changes; no if → add.
- test-core: needs changes; no if → add.
- integration-mock: AND.
- hostile-env: AND (single line).
- fa-aot-build: no needs; add needs + if.
- pty-integration-linux: needs [fa-aot-build]; no if → add.
- pty-coverage-gate: needs [pty-integration-linux]; no if → add.
- pty-visual: needs changes; no if → add.
- coverage-gate: needs [changes, test-core]; no if → add.
- guards: needs [changes, test-core]; no if → add.
- flutter-analyze: AND.
- flutter-tests: AND.
- flutter-app-exzone: folded if → append line `      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` — wait, folded `>-` with `||` structure: append `&& (...)`? The block is:
```
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-shot: wire the gh-1551 release-pending guard into ci.yml gate legs."""
import re, sys

path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')

GUARD = "needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
COMMENT = ('    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* '
           'tag)\n    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check '
           'decides.')

# job -> ('and' | 'new' | 'fold_wrap' | 'always_and')
plan = {
    'cube-kernel-live': 'and',
    'static': 'new',
    'test-core': 'new',
    'integration-mock': 'and',
    'hostile-env': 'and',
    'fa-aot-build': 'new_noneeds',
    'pty-integration-linux': 'new',
    'pty-coverage-gate': 'new',
    'pty-visual': 'new',
    'coverage-gate': 'new',
    'guards': 'new',
    'flutter-analyze': 'and',
    'flutter-tests': 'and',
    'flutter-app-exzone': 'fold_wrap',
    'app-crap-gate': 'and',
    'test-faui': 'and',
    'faui-coverage': 'new',
    'cli-visual-settings': 'and',
    'build-web': 'and',
    'build-android': 'and',
    'build-ios': 'and',
    'build-macos': 'and',
    'supply-chain': 'new',
    'dep-audit': 'new',
    'installer-verify': 'new',
    'install-pin-gate': 'new',
    'quality-gate': 'always_and',
    'perf-gate': 'and',
    'usage-fold': 'fold_wrap',
    'step-timings': 'always_and',
    'js-ext-integration': 'new',
    'release': 'release_fold',
}

# find job header line indices
headers = {}
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r'^  ([a-z0-9-]+):$', l)
    if m:
        headers[m.group(1)] = i

def find_line(start, indent, key):
    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
        if re.match(r'^  [a-z0-9-]+:$', lines[j]) and j > start:
            return None
        if lines[j].startswith(f'{indent}{key}:'):
            return j
    return None

edits = []  # (lineno, kind, payload)

for job, mode in plan.items():
    h = headers[job]
    nline = find_line(h, '    ', 'needs')
    iline = find_line(h, '    ', 'if')
    if nline is None:
        if mode == 'new_noneeds':
            edits.append((h + 1, 'insert', f'    needs: release-pending'))
        else:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: expected a needs line')
    else:
        cur = lines[nline].strip()[len('needs:'):].strip()
        if 'release-pending' in cur:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: already wired?')
        if cur.startswith('['):
            new = 'needs: [release-pending, ' + cur[1:]
        else:
            new = f'needs: [release-pending, {cur}]'
        edits.append((nline, 'replace', new))

    if mode == 'and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur.startswith('if:'), cur
        expr = cur[len('if:'):].strip()
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: {expr} && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode in ('new', 'new_noneeds'):
        target = nline if nline is not None else h + 1
        edits.append((target, 'insert_after',
                      f'{COMMENT}\n    if: {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'always_and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur == 'if: always()', cur
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: always() && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'fold_wrap':
        assert lines[iline].strip() == 'if: >-', (job, lines[iline])
        # find block extent
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        first_expr = iline + 1
        edits.append((first_expr, 'replace',
                      '(' + lines[first_expr].strip()))
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ') &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'release_fold':
        # append guard as a new folded line at the end of the if block
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ' &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    else:
        sys.exit(f'unknown mode {mode}')

# apply edits bottom-up, tracking insert positions
edits.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], 0 if e[1] == 'replace' else 1))
out = list(lines)
for lineno, kind, payload in sorted(edits, key=lambda e: -e[0] if e[1] == 'replace' else -(e[0] + 0.5)):
    pass  # handled below

# Simpler: apply in reverse line order; inserts before/after anchored at the
# (possibly already edited) line. Since replace and insert share anchors,
# process per anchor in a stable way.
from collections import defaultdict
by_line = defaultdict(list)
for lineno, kind, payload in edits:
    by_line[lineno].append((kind, payload))

result = []
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if i in by_line:
        for kind, payload in by_line[i]:
            if kind == 'replace':
                line = '    ' + payload if not payload.startswith('    ') else payload
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('(') or payload.lstrip().startswith('needs.'):
                    line = '      ' + payload if 'needs.' in payload[:8] or payload.lstrip().startswith('(') else '    ' + payload
            # collects handled below
        # re-derive: we must keep replace-1 + insert_after ordering
    result.append(line)

# The above in-place juggling is error-prone; rebuild cleanly instead.
result = []
i = 0
n = len(lines)
while i < n:
    line = lines[i]
    if i in by_line:
        ops = by_line[i]
        indent = '    '
        replaced = None
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'replace':
                # preserve original indentation of the anchor line
                orig_indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('needs:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                elif payload.lstrip().startswith('if:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                else:
                    # folded if expression line: 6-space indent
                    replaced = f'      {payload}'
        if replaced is not None:
            result.append(replaced)
        else:
            result.append(line)
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'insert':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
            elif kind == 'insert_after':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
        i += 1
        continue
    result.append(line)
    i += 1

open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(result))
print('applied', len(edits), 'edits across', len(plan), 'jobs')

There's a BUG: `||` expressions got the guard appended without parentheses:

`needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`

Due to `&&` binding tighter than `||`, this evaluates as `core || (shared && pending)` — WRONG! If core=true and pending=false, the leg would still RUN. Must wrap: `(core || shared) && pending`.

Affected jobs with `||` in single-line ifs: hostile-env, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, cli-visual-settings, build-web/android/ios/macos. integration-mock has no `||` (single condition) ✓. cube-kernel-live single ✓.

Fix: wrap the original expression in parens.

path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'

        lines[i] = f"{m.group(1)}({m.group(2)}) && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
        fixed += 1
open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
print('fixed', fixed)
EOF"}

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410b181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"
          fi
          echo "release pending: $pending"
          echo "pending=$pending" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-shot: wire the gh-1551 release-pending guard into ci.yml gate legs."""
import re, sys

path = '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
lines = open(path).read().split('\n')

GUARD = "needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
COMMENT = ('    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* '
           'tag)\n    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check '
           'decides.')

# job -> ('and' | 'new' | 'fold_wrap' | 'always_and')
plan = {
    'cube-kernel-live': 'and',
    'static': 'new',
    'test-core': 'new',
    'integration-mock': 'and',
    'hostile-env': 'and',
    'fa-aot-build': 'new_noneeds',
    'pty-integration-linux': 'new',
    'pty-coverage-gate': 'new',
    'pty-visual': 'new',
    'coverage-gate': 'new',
    'guards': 'new',
    'flutter-analyze': 'and',
    'flutter-tests': 'and',
    'flutter-app-exzone': 'fold_wrap',
    'app-crap-gate': 'and',
    'test-faui': 'and',
    'faui-coverage': 'new',
    'cli-visual-settings': 'and',
    'build-web': 'and',
    'build-android': 'and',
    'build-ios': 'and',
    'build-macos': 'and',
    'supply-chain': 'new',
    'dep-audit': 'new',
    'installer-verify': 'new',
    'install-pin-gate': 'new',
    'quality-gate': 'always_and',
    'perf-gate': 'and',
    'usage-fold': 'fold_wrap',
    'step-timings': 'always_and',
    'js-ext-integration': 'new',
    'release': 'release_fold',
}

# find job header line indices
headers = {}
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.match(r'^  ([a-z0-9-]+):$', l)
    if m:
        headers[m.group(1)] = i

def find_line(start, indent, key):
    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
        if re.match(r'^  [a-z0-9-]+:$', lines[j]) and j > start:
            return None
        if lines[j].startswith(f'{indent}{key}:'):
            return j
    return None

edits = []  # (lineno, kind, payload)

for job, mode in plan.items():
    h = headers[job]
    nline = find_line(h, '    ', 'needs')
    iline = find_line(h, '    ', 'if')
    if nline is None:
        if mode == 'new_noneeds':
            edits.append((h + 1, 'insert', f'    needs: release-pending'))
        else:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: expected a needs line')
    else:
        cur = lines[nline].strip()[len('needs:'):].strip()
        if 'release-pending' in cur:
            sys.exit(f'{job}: already wired?')
        if cur.startswith('['):
            new = 'needs: [release-pending, ' + cur[1:]
        else:
            new = f'needs: [release-pending, {cur}]'
        edits.append((nline, 'replace', new))

    if mode == 'and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur.startswith('if:'), cur
        expr = cur[len('if:'):].strip()
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: {expr} && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode in ('new', 'new_noneeds'):
        target = nline if nline is not None else h + 1
        edits.append((target, 'insert_after',
                      f'{COMMENT}\n    if: {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'always_and':
        assert iline is not None, job
        cur = lines[iline].strip()
        assert cur == 'if: always()', cur
        edits.append((iline, 'replace', f'if: always() && {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'fold_wrap':
        assert lines[iline].strip() == 'if: >-', (job, lines[iline])
        # find block extent
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        first_expr = iline + 1
        edits.append((first_expr, 'replace',
                      '(' + lines[first_expr].strip()))
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ') &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    elif mode == 'release_fold':
        # append guard as a new folded line at the end of the if block
        j = iline + 1
        while lines[j].startswith('      '):
            j += 1
        last = j - 1
        edits.append((last, 'replace',
                      lines[last].strip() + ' &&'))
        edits.append((last, 'insert_after', f'      {GUARD}'))
    else:
        sys.exit(f'unknown mode {mode}')

# apply edits bottom-up, tracking insert positions
edits.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], 0 if e[1] == 'replace' else 1))
out = list(lines)
for lineno, kind, payload in sorted(edits, key=lambda e: -e[0] if e[1] == 'replace' else -(e[0] + 0.5)):
    pass  # handled below

# Simpler: apply in reverse line order; inserts before/after anchored at the
# (possibly already edited) line. Since replace and insert share anchors,
# process per anchor in a stable way.
from collections import defaultdict
by_line = defaultdict(list)
for lineno, kind, payload in edits:
    by_line[lineno].append((kind, payload))

result = []
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if i in by_line:
        for kind, payload in by_line[i]:
            if kind == 'replace':
                line = '    ' + payload if not payload.startswith('    ') else payload
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('(') or payload.lstrip().startswith('needs.'):
                    line = '      ' + payload if 'needs.' in payload[:8] or payload.lstrip().startswith('(') else '    ' + payload
            # collects handled below
        # re-derive: we must keep replace-1 + insert_after ordering
    result.append(line)

# The above in-place juggling is error-prone; rebuild cleanly instead.
result = []
i = 0
n = len(lines)
while i < n:
    line = lines[i]
    if i in by_line:
        ops = by_line[i]
        indent = '    '
        replaced = None
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'replace':
                # preserve original indentation of the anchor line
                orig_indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
                if payload.lstrip().startswith('needs:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                elif payload.lstrip().startswith('if:'):
                    replaced = f'{orig_indent}{payload}'
                else:
                    # folded if expression line: 6-space indent
                    replaced = f'      {payload}'
        if replaced is not None:
            result.append(replaced)
        else:
            result.append(line)
        for kind, payload in ops:
            if kind == 'insert':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
            elif kind == 'insert_after':
                result.extend(payload.split('\n'))
        i += 1
        continue
    result.append(line)
    i += 1

open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(result))
print('applied', len(edits), 'edits across', len(plan), 'jobs')

+              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"

There's a BUG: `||` expressions got the guard appended without parentheses:

`needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'`

Due to `&&` binding tighter than `||`, this evaluates as `core || (shared && pending)` — WRONG! If core=true and pending=false, the leg would still RUN. Must wrap: `(core || shared) && pending`.

Affected jobs with `||` in single-line ifs: hostile-env, flutter-analyze, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, cli-visual-settings, build-web/android/ios/macos. integration-mock has no `||` (single condition) ✓. cube-kernel-live single ✓.

Fix: wrap the original expression in parens.

        lines[i] = f"{m.group(1)}({m.group(2)}) && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'"
        fixed += 1
open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
print('fixed', fixed)
EOF"}
